Subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan & success criteria (post-call recap)

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC kicked off quickly: 

Summary of ask
- Acme wants to validate a customer-facing summarization flow for support tickets (multi-turn context) at scale.
- Key constraints: latency sensitivity for first-response (target 95th percentile) and high factual correctness for ticket resolution suggestions.

Proposed POC (4 weeks) — high level
- Week 0: Kickoff + environment setup (dataset ingestion, access, test keys)
- Week 1: Offline evals on holdout set + initial model tuning
- Week 2: Shadow (online) run against 10% traffic for 48–72 hours
- Week 3: Stabilization, A/B, and final evaluation + handoff

Success criteria (proposed)
- Quality: >= 85% on our graded rubric (accuracy & helpfulness combined) on offline evals
- Latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for inference on the target payload distribution
- Cost: expected per-1M-token unit cost within the committed range (we'll model after initial runs)
- Ops: no P0 incidents during shadow; error rate < 0.5%

Ownership
- Acme: data access, holdout dataset, business sign-off on acceptance rubric (Priya)
- Redwood: model provisioning, eval harness, shadow routing, and instrumentation (Dylan/Marissa)

Attachments
- evaluation_plan_draft.pdf (attached) — draft eval plan, dataset spec, and proposed instrumentation.

Next steps
1) Priya / Alex: confirm success criteria above or provide adjustments by EOD Wed 2026-06-03
2) Redwood: finalize the eval rubric & plan and share updated doc (Marissa)
3) Schedule kickoff (30–45m) once criteria are agreed — suggest Thu 2026-06-04 morning PT

If anything above doesn't match your expectation, call it out and we'll update.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Thanks for the clear recap, Dylan — appreciate the timeline. A few quick items from our side: 

- Overall looks good; we agree with a 4-week approach.
- Quality target: we want to set the acceptance threshold a bit higher — can we aim for >= 88% on the rubric? We can be flexible if the rubric is conservative.
- Evaluation methodology: we prefer an online shadow run (production traffic shadowed) as the primary signal, with offline evals used for early filtering. Our platform is pretty stable and we can route ~10% of traffic to shadow during the test window.
- Grading: can you share a proposed grading rubric (how you score accuracy/helpfulness, and how disagreement is adjudicated)? We have a small labeling team that can do adjudication if needed.

We can confirm criteria by EOD Wed 2026-06-03 provided we see the rubric. Also happy to do kickoff Thu morning PT — Alex, Priya prefer 10:00–11:00 PT if available.

Thanks — good notes. Quick response on methodology and rubric so Priya / Alex can see what we propose: 

Recommended approach (hybrid)
- Offline evals first to verify baseline model behavior on curated holdout (precision, recall, hallucination rate). This helps us catch obvious regressions and tune prompts/temperature without touching prod.
- Short online shadow (48–72h at 10% traffic) for real-signal evaluation on latency, stability, and emergent failure modes (we've seen edge cases only in shadow runs).

Grading rubric (high level) — we'll share a spreadsheet (attached: acme_poc_eval_rubric.xlsx) with examples and scoring details, but summary: 
- Accuracy (0–5): factual correctness of suggested resolution relative to ticket text and known facts (weighted 50%)
- Helpfulness / Actionability (0–3): whether the suggested action lets an agent resolve or triage faster (weighted 30%)
- Safety / Appropriateness (0–2): no PII leakage, no unsafe suggestions (weighted 20%)
- Composite score normalized to 100; pass threshold (proposed): >= 88% (per Priya's ask) — can be tuned with Adjudication.

Adjudication process
- If annotator disagreement > 20% on a given example, we escalate to a small adjudication panel (1 Acme SME + 1 Redwood SME) to decide final label.

Ownership & deliverables
- Redwood: provide rubric template, automated eval harness, and a dashboard with per-bucket breakdown (Marissa)
- Acme: provide holdout set, adjudication SME, and sign-off on final pass/fail

Next steps (updated)
1) Redwood: share updated evaluation_plan_draft.pdf and rubric spreadsheet (attached) by EOD Tue 2026-06-02
2) Acme: confirm acceptance threshold (88%) + availability for Thursday 10:00 PT kickoff
3) Redwood: provision shadow keys and traffic config ahead of kickoff

I'll attach the rubric spreadsheet for clarity. If everyone is aligned I'll convert this to a short mutual action plan after kickoff.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
